title: Blower Motor Speed Control
introduction:
The blower motor moves cabin air; the speed-control module adjusts its electrical drive in response to the climate controls. Think of the module as the fan’s dimmer switch: it sets the pace while the motor does the spinning. I keep that distinction clear when identifying the part beneath the RH side of the instrument panel.

This guide covers access, removal and refitting of the speed-control module. The drawings lead from the insulation panel and its ambient light to the connector beside the blower housing, then to the module’s locking tab and sliding mount. They provide a replacement route, without establishing that this component caused an airflow complaint.

items.name: Prevent unexpected starting
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Protect eyes, ears and hands
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged components. Failure to use this protection may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Review the applicable safety references
items.detail: Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) and [Climate Control System Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693184) before starting. The supplied module-removal sequence involves the insulation panel, electrical connection and sliding mount; it requires no refrigerant or heater-hose disconnection.

items.name: Locate the module from below
items.detail: Work beneath the RH side of the instrument panel. The insulation panel covers the access area; behind it, the speed-control connector sits beside the round blower housing. Have a non-marring trim tool available, as shown in the connector-release illustration.

edits.text: Remove the push pins and lower the RH insulation panel for removal, freeing its ambient light as described below.
edits.why: The panel sits beneath the instrument panel. Taking it down opens access to the blower housing and speed-control module; the ambient light must be released before the panel can be taken away.

edits.text: Turn the insulation-panel ambient-light unit in the direction of the curved arrow in the inset, then remove it from the panel’s circular opening.
edits.why: Viewed from the exposed underside of the insulation panel, turn the ambient-light fitting counterclockwise to release it, then withdraw it from the opening. Support the panel until the fitting is free so its weight does not pull on the light wiring.

edits.text: Release and disconnect the blower motor speed control connector, then move the wiring harness aside.
edits.why: The connector is beside the round blower housing. The drawing includes a non-marring trim tool for releasing its lock. Moving the harness clear leaves room for the module’s sliding removal movement.

edits.text: Press down on the lock tab at the top of the blower motor speed control module to release it.
edits.why: The highlighted tab holds the module in its sliding mount. Release that catch before attempting to move the module sideways.

edits.text: Slide the blower motor speed control module to the right, as viewed in the close-up, then remove it from its mount.
edits.why: The sideways movement disengages the mounting features after the tab has been released. It is a slide-and-release attachment, so pulling straight out before sliding would work against the mount.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: place the blower motor speed control module into its mount, slide it left to engage the lock tab, return the wiring harness and reconnect the connector. Reinstall the ambient-light unit in the insulation panel, then refit the RH insulation panel and its push pins.
edits.why:
The completed refit leaves the module retained by its lock tab, the connector engaged and the harness clear of the mounting area. Insert the ambient-light fitting into the panel opening and turn it clockwise when viewed from the exposed underside, then secure the panel.

After all reassembly, remove tools and clear hands from the blower and wiring. Keep the car parked in P for an automatic or a parked gear for a manual, with the parking brake applied, wheels chocked and engine stopped. With the valid intelligent access key inside, press and release START/STOP from confirmed OFF without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. With Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC), vary the blower switch and confirm airflow changes. With Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC), use the blower override buttons to select different speeds. See the [EMTC controls](#/document/G1681091) and [DATC controls](#/document/G1676851). This is an ordinary completion check, not a test of every climate-control function. If airflow remains unresponsive, switch the climate controls and ignition OFF and remove the key before checking the connection disturbed during this job. If installation is secure and the complaint remains, continue the matching system diagnosis rather than guessing at another part. After a successful check, also turn the climate controls off, then press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to return known ON to OFF and remove the key.

editorialRevision.scope: Only requirements/why increments; primary mechanical texts unchanged. Direct source figure establishes CCW release/CW refit from underside. Owner-backed keyless engine-off ordinary fan-speed completion, not diagnostic threshold or refrigerant work.
